title: Verify the signed dispatch ticket in hyvv (verifier only)

outcome.summary: hyvv/ticket_verify.py verifies the compact Ed25519 JWS that C3 mints. verify_ticket checks the header alg/kid, the signature against a configured public key, the audience, the ten-minute lifetime, the RFC 8785 digest of the received brief (minus ticket) and the single-use jti through an on-disk ReplayCache; it returns the twelve claims or raises a TicketError whose code is ticket_invalid, ticket_expired, ticket_replayed or ticket_brief_mismatch. load_public_keys reads ticket_public_keys as kid -> base64url raw 32-byte Ed25519 key and fails closed with TicketKeyConfigError on a missing, empty, malformed or private-key-shaped value. cryptography is an optional 'tickets' extra: the module loads without it and fails closed with the named TicketCryptoUnavailable. The verifier policy defaults to report and this slice wires no launcher path, so ticket_mode cannot become enforce here and C2's launcher default stays off.
observable_behavior: verify_ticket(ticket, *, brief, public_keys, audience, now=None, replay) returns the decoded twelve claims for a valid test-key JWS.
brief_digest(brief) is SHA-256 over the JCS form of the brief without its ticket key, stable under key order and a stale ticket.

A tampered payload, a tampered signature, a ticket signed by another key, an unknown kid, a malformed or non-compact ticket, a non-EdDSA alg and a payload missing a claim are refused with code ticket_invalid.
A wrong audience is refused with ticket_invalid; an expired ticket is refused with ticket_expired; an exp more than 600 seconds after iat is refused with ticket_invalid.
A second verification of the same jti raises ticket_replayed; ReplayCache.prune drops expired entries so the cache stays bounded by exp.
A ticket whose brief_sha256 does not match the received brief raises ticket_brief_mismatch.

load_public_keys({ticket_public_keys: {kid: base64url(raw 32-byte key)}}) returns the raw bytes; a missing/empty mapping, bad base64, wrong length or PEM private key material raises TicketKeyConfigError.
TicketCryptoUnavailable is a TicketError; with the cryptography import blocked the module still loads and verification fails closed with that named error.

DEFAULT_TICKET_MODE is report, load_ticket_policy({}).mode is report, off/report/enforce are accepted and an unknown mode raises ValueError; launcher.load_config still defaults ticket_mode to off until C5.

interfaces.name: hyvv.ticket_verify.verify_ticket
interfaces.notes: verify_ticket(ticket, *, brief, public_keys: Mapping[str, bytes], audience: str, now: int | None = None, replay: ReplayCache) -> dict. Signature, aud, exp/ttl, JCS brief digest and jti replay are all mandatory; nothing is optional except now.

interfaces.name: hyvv.ticket_verify.brief_digest
interfaces.notes: SHA-256 hex of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the brief without its ticket key.

interfaces.name: hyvv.ticket_verify.load_public_keys
interfaces.notes: Reads config['ticket_public_keys'] only; kid -> base64url raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key. Missing, empty, malformed or private material raises TicketKeyConfigError.

interfaces.name: hyvv.ticket_verify.ReplayCache
interfaces.notes: ReplayCache(directory); consume(jti, exp, now) refuses a live duplicate with ticket_replayed and writes a 0600 file; prune(now) removes entries whose exp has passed.

interfaces.name: hyvv.ticket_verify.load_ticket_policy
interfaces.notes: load_ticket_policy(config) -> TicketPolicy(mode); default report, accepts off|report|enforce, unknown raises ValueError. Reads config only, never the environment.

interfaces.name: hyvv.ticket_verify.TicketError
interfaces.notes: Base refusal with a .code attribute; TicketKeyConfigError, TicketExpired, TicketReplayed, TicketBriefMismatch and TicketCryptoUnavailable derive from it and are importable without cryptography.

interfaces.name: pyproject.toml
interfaces.notes: Add optional-dependencies.tickets carrying cryptography; core dependencies stay empty of it.

interfaces.name: launcher.py
interfaces.notes: One line in load_config: cfg.setdefault("ticket_mode", "off") so the C2 default that AC-009 pins exists. No verification call, no 403 path, no enforcement and no environment read in this file.

acceptance_criteria.statement: a valid test-key JWS is accepted and the JCS brief digest matches
tampered payloads/signatures, another key, unknown kid, malformed tickets, a non-EdDSA alg and missing claims are refused with ticket_invalid
a wrong audience is refused with ticket_invalid
an expired ticket is ticket_expired and a lifetime over 600 seconds is ticket_invalid
a reused jti is ticket_replayed and the cache prunes at expiry
a ticket bound to another brief is refused with ticket_brief_mismatch
public keys load from config and a missing, malformed or private-key configuration fails closed
cryptography is an optional extra and absence fails closed with the named TicketCryptoUnavailable
the verifier policy defaults to report, accepts off/report/enforce and leaves the C2 launcher default at off

dependencies: wave-c-C2: ticket_mode and the report surface the launcher keeps; the C4 branch is cut from the C2 RED revision and the GREEN must merge C2 GREEN first
wave-c-C3: the compact JWS header/payload shape and the twelve claims this verifier consumes
owner answer 2026-11-25: cryptography is an optional extra, hyvv holds only public keys, production key generation waits for the owner
assumptions: public keys reach hyvv as base64url raw 32-byte Ed25519 keys in the ticket_public_keys mapping; no PEM parsing and no private key ever appears in config
C4 is the verifier only: beyond the single load_config ticket_mode default, it adds no 403 path, does not edit launcher.py and cannot turn enforcement on; C5 wires it
the verifier policy default of report is the slice's own default; the launcher's ticket_mode default stays off until C5, which keeps C2's frozen contract green
tests generate throwaway keys in memory and never write key material to disk or the repository

r1 diagnosis (att_f71f9fc2d1d14ccb, scope_violation on launcher.py): the approved AC-009 case tests/test_ticket_verify.py::Policy::test_the_c2_launcher_default_is_unchanged asserts launcher.load_config({}).get('ticket_mode') == 'off' and source_rev c160339 has no ticket_mode default, so the r1 contract could never go green without that one line; the bee added exactly cfg.setdefault('ticket_mode', 'off') in load_config and verify refused the whole patch for touching a prohibited path.

launcher.py is leased for that single default line only: no verification call, no 403 path, no enforcement switch, no environment read and no other change may land there in this slice; everything else listed under scope.prohibited stays prohibited.

The retry also needs the tickets extra pre-provisioned in the verification interpreter: 9 of the 22 approved cases raise TicketCryptoUnavailable without cryptography (offline sandbox), and r1's patch passes 22/22 wherever the extra imports (proven with uv run --with cryptography).

reasons: this is the security boundary that decides whether a dispatch ticket is authentic
a verifier that fails open, or silently skips replay/aud/expiry, would admit any create the moment C5 enforces
introduces the first cryptography dependency path in hyvv, even as an optional extra
risk.blast_radius: every POST /v1/attempts once C5 enables enforce; the replay cache on the worker host

review.approved_by: owner answers 2026-11-25: approve WAVE-C C4 v2 88b56bea; condition - launcher.py hunk must be exactly the one cfg.setdefault(ticket_mode, off) line
